newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 6.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 6.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to large ships on Friday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.
Strong winds along the Pacific Coast kept the largely tourist ports of Huatulco and Puerto Madero shut to smaller tourism and fishing craft for the fourth day in a row.
The SCT's alert for shipping along the Pacific was lifted as Andres turned into a tropical depression and waned along the Nicaraguan coast. The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings
for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
In the Baja California region, winds in the north from 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves five to eight feet high because a weak cold front.
Along the southern coast, winds had relaxed to 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves four to six feet high.
Cold front expected to bring rains later in the day, winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves three to five feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with scattered rains. Winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
